operations.specification: This API endpoint enables new customer registration within the shopping-mall platform. It creates a new customer account by accepting user-provided registration details such as email and password, and persists these fields in the shopping_mall_customers table. Upon a successful registration, this operation issues initial JWT tokens that authenticate future API usage for this customer. The registration process is fully aligned with the 'member' actor pattern as specified by requirements. The endpoint handles input validation for email uniqueness (matching the 'email' field's unique constraint in schema) and password complexity requirements as described in business rules. Security considerations include using password hashing and transactional integrity for customer creation as mandated by security policy. In the business workflow, this operation is the starting point for any customer who wants to browse, purchase, or interact with the system beyond guest access. It is related to the authentication and token refresh operations that complete the customer authentication lifecycle. All referenced fields (email, password) are confirmed present in the shopping_mall_customers schema; no registration is possible without these fields being provided by the user.
operations.description:
This operation registers a new customer account based on user-supplied credentials, storing key identity fields in the shopping_mall_customers table. Email uniqueness is enforced per schema constraints. Successful registration returns JWT tokens for immediate use, transforming an unauthenticated visitor into a full 'member' actor as defined in platform requirements.

During execution, input is validated for essential fields including email and password, referencing the schema's unique and required constraints. Password is securely hashed prior to storage, and email must be unique; duplicate attempts trigger appropriate error responses.

Account is created inside a transaction to ensure data integrity. The operation does not assign additional roles or permissions at this stage, but it does activate the core customer identity in the system.

Security is a priority: passwords are never exposed, and JWT is returned in the expected API response structure—see requirements for security and compliance details. The join flow is the gateway for future login or refresh actions.

Related endpoints include login (credential verification post-registration) and token refresh (session renewal), both forming the rest of the customer authentication lifecycle and requiring this registration as a prerequisite.
operations.summary: Registers a new customer by creating a member account in shopping_mall_customers and returning JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Registration details for new customer account. Schema fields must match shopping_mall_customers model (e.g., email, password).

responseBody.description: Authorized response including issued JWT access and refresh tokens for new customer session.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: This API endpoint authenticates a registered customer by verifying provided credentials (email and password) against stored records in the shopping_mall_customers table. On successful verification, it issues a new set of JWT tokens using the standard authentication workflow for the 'member' actor. This operation relies on fields 'email' and 'password' confirmed to exist in the schema. It responds with structured error handling for failed authentication, including locked accounts or invalid credentials. Business rules for authentication—such as login attempt throttling, account lockout after multiple failures (if specified in requirements), and password verification logic—are referenced directly from the associated schema and business documentation. Security practices include secure password comparison, issuing JWT access and refresh tokens on success, and not exposing sensitive information in error responses. This operation is essential to enable access to protected customer features and is a central workflow for returning authenticated customers after registration.
operations.description:
This operation enables customer login via email and password authentication, referencing required fields in the shopping_mall_customers schema. Provided credentials are verified; correct input issues fresh JWT access and refresh tokens. Unsuccessful attempts, such as invalid credentials or locked-out accounts, use schema constraints and requirements-driven error messaging.

Authentication logic enforces password hashing and secure comparison methods per platform security requirements. If login attempt limits or lockout states exist in schema, these are handled as described, returning errors for exceeded limits or inactive accounts.

Login is the principal mechanism for customers to authenticate to protected endpoints, re-using their registration identity. The process never returns password hashes and all error messages are generic to avoid information leakage.

Tied directly to the registration (join) and refresh endpoints, this completes the authentication cycle required for secure platform access. Only registered users with valid credentials are authenticated.

The schema explicitly provides both 'email' and 'password' fields, required for any customer login, and implementation uses these without assumption.
operations.summary: Authenticates customer credentials against shopping_mall_customers and returns a new JWT token set.

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials—must match required fields in shopping_mall_customers (e.g., email, password).

responseBody.description: Authorized response containing fresh JWT access and refresh tokens on successful authentication.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: This endpoint renews JWT access and refresh tokens for an already authenticated customer. It implements the token refresh functionality by validating a provided refresh token (which must correspond to a valid and unexpired entry in shopping_mall_customer_sessions). On successful verification, a new access token is returned, prolonging the customer session according to authentication workflow rules. The refresh logic strictly adheres to the 'member' actor pattern and references the existence of session tokens in schema ('shopping_mall_customer_sessions'). Error handling follows requirements—expired/invalid tokens are handled gracefully and according to compliance. This operation complements join and login as a lifecycle phase for active sessions. Implementation ensures secure handling of refresh tokens, never exposing details in responses and rotating tokens as necessary to prevent replay attacks. The prerequisite for this endpoint is an active refresh token corresponding to a legitimate customer session as recorded in the database.
operations.description:
This operation allows a customer to refresh JWT access and refresh tokens, using the session tracking and token rotation logic keyed to shopping_mall_customer_sessions. A valid refresh token must be provided, and token validity is checked against session records for expiration or revocation.

The schema includes mechanisms for recording and managing sessions, which are leveraged here for compliance and audit. Expired or invalid tokens generate specific error responses without revealing information that could aid attackers.

The endpoint is critical in allowing customers to seamlessly maintain authenticated sessions in accordance with platform security requirements.

The process is fully integrated with authentication workflows established in requirements, using both join and login as prerequisites for having issued refresh tokens in the first place.

All token management operations are based on schema-supported session structures, ensuring correctness of the refresh logic and recordkeeping.
operations.summary: Refreshes a customer's JWT tokens upon receipt of valid refresh token, using shopping_mall_customer_sessions.

requestBody.description: Refresh token object as per session schema for customer.

responseBody.description: Authorized response with new JWT access and refresh tokens after refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation registers a new seller account on the shopping mall platform. It creates a new seller record in the database and issues an initial access token for immediate authenticated interaction. The request body matches the seller registration DTO, which must include fields required by the Prisma schema's shopping_mall_sellers table. The endpoint is designed for unauthenticated access so that prospective sellers can onboard themselves. The response includes a JWT access/refresh token pair as described in authentication specifications. This operation enables platform expansion by lowering the barrier to seller onboarding. Security measures such as password strength enforcement, email uniqueness, and validation against the relevant schema fields are applied. Failure responses are triggered in cases such as email duplication or insufficient data, with clear error messages per seller authentication policies and database constraints. Registration is the foundation for all subsequent seller authentication and management actions. This operation must reference only those fields that exist in the seller Prisma schema. Successful registration is required before login or any further seller functions can be used.
operations.description:
This API registers a new seller account in the platform. It accepts registration details necessary for a seller, as defined in the database schema (shopping_mall_sellers), such as email, password, and other required fields. On success, it creates a seller entity and issues authentication tokens for immediate seller dashboard or API use.

All validation logic—such as unique email/username, password policy, and fulfillment of required schema fields—is applied to prevent duplicate accounts and enforce security. The seller registration flow is unauthenticated and permits onboarding for new marketplace merchants.

This operation initiates the authentication lifecycle for the actor of kind 'member', forming the basis for future logins and privileged actions. Tokens returned follow the IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized DTO documented in the service.

Security considerations: rate limiting, anti-automation (CAPTCHA/throttle), and strong password requirements should be enabled. Sensitive data (password) must be securely transmitted and never exposed in logs or error payloads.

Any business logic linked to new account creation (e.g., send verification mail, initiate approval process) must reference only actual fields present in the seller table of the schema. This ensures compliance with functional requirements and minimizes onboarding risk.
operations.summary: Register a new seller account in the shopping_mall_sellers table and issue a JWT token pair.

requestBody.description: Seller registration request body

responseBody.description: Authentication result object

operations.name: join

operations.specification: This operation authenticates a seller actor using credential fields defined in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma schema (e.g., email and password if defined as columns). It issues a JWT access and refresh token pair upon successful authentication. This is the entry point for registered sellers to access protected seller features. Only credentials actually defined in the shopping_mall_sellers table (and in the authentication DTO) are permitted for login; do not assume fields beyond those present in schema. The endpoint is publicly accessible for credential submission, and results in either authenticated tokens or descriptive failure errors. Implementation must ensure secure comparison of authentication secrets, prevent timing attacks, and limit failed attempts according to platform security policy. Successful login is required for session creation and seller feature access. The returned response follows authentication data transfer object and naming conventions.
operations.description:
This API allows sellers to authenticate using credentials defined in the seller database schema (shopping_mall_sellers), such as email and password. The operation verifies credentials against stored records, handling all error states for incorrect password, missing account, or locked/disabled seller statuses using only those fields present in schema.

On success, it issues JWT access and refresh tokens as described by the IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized DTO. This is the canonical login entrypoint for all seller account activity.

Security controls include throttling on repeated failed login attempts, secure password transmission, and ensuring only required data fields (as per schema and DTO) are accepted in the request body. No extraneous profile or non-auth fields are accepted.

Login is a public operation (authorizationActor: null) but all subsequent authenticated business operations require valid tokens, linking this operation to the seller login session lifecycle and session storage if schemas for session or audit logs exist.

All referenced credential fields must be verified to exist in the shopping_mall_sellers table, and the login handler may NOT assume standard fields if they are absent from the schema.
operations.summary: Authenticate a seller and issue a JWT token pair using schema-defined login credentials.

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials (schema-defined)

responseBody.description: Authentication result object

operations.name: login

operations.specification: This operation refreshes expired or near-expiry JWT-based tokens for an authenticated seller actor. It accepts a refresh token and, if valid, issues a new access/refresh token pair as per the authentication DTO. The operation requires that a valid seller session exists, and the refresh token matches the appropriate structure and signing rules. Only schemas referencing seller session or token management (if present) should be referenced here. Do NOT assume refresh session storage if no session table is present in Prisma; simply validate token cryptographically. Errors are clearly reported for expired, malformed, or tampered tokens following security policy. The returned type follows the authorized DTO standard for sellers. This endpoint is actor-agnostic in path structure, and authentication context is established solely from the provided refresh token. Token refresh is essential for seamless session continuity and secure token lifecycle management for sellers. Only real schema support should be referenced in prerequisites or operation logic.
operations.description:
This API accepts a valid refresh token, as defined in the authentication DTO for sellers, and issues a new JWT access/refresh token pair if the refresh token is valid. It implements token rotation and advanced security controls such as issued-at/expiration checks, scope/claim verification, and rotation logics if a refresh session table exists in the schema.

On success, it returns the new tokens as IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized response. Token renewal is critical for seamless authentication retention by seller actors using long-lived dashboard/API sessions, and the implementation should not go beyond schema support for session/token storage.

The operation fails with clear errors on attempt to use expired, reused, or cryptographically invalid tokens. This endpoint does not require an authenticated context (authorizationActor: null) because authentication is performed via cryptographic token validation.

Security notes: all refresh token logic uses only schema-supported session/token features, with no reference to features unsupported by the schema. This ensures security policy alignment and DTO compatibility.

For sellers, refresh is required for persistent session management and security; it is a mandatory part of the authentication lifecycle.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for seller, issuing new access/refresh token pair if the refresh token is valid.

requestBody.description: Refresh token request body for seller

responseBody.description: Authentication result object

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification:
This operation enables platform administrators to register an admin account on the platform and receive initial authentication tokens. It directly relates to the 'shopping_mall_admins' Prisma table, supporting the onboarding of new admin users. The endpoint collects required registration credentials (such as username and password fields defined in the admin schema) and provisions an admin user record with all necessary default fields. Upon successful registration, the operation responds with JWT tokens referencing the 'IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized' type.

This join flow ensures that all required fields (from the schema, e.g., email, password, admin_name, etc.) are validated and stored appropriately. The system applies strict validation according to field constraints (such as unique email or required password complexity specified in the Prisma schema or business rules). After successful creation, the response includes the necessary authentication payload for subsequent operations using the issued token pairs.

This operation is public, allowing onboarding of authorized platform administrators. Security controls prevent mass registrations or unauthorized elevation. The operation only provisions fields available and specified in the 'shopping_mall_admins' table.

Error handling covers duplicate registration, validation failures (including schema-level unique fields, e.g., email), and system errors. Related operations include admin login and token refresh flows.
operations.description:
This API operation allows registration of new admin accounts into the system by collecting required credentials such as username, email, and password, as specified in the 'shopping_mall_admins' Prisma schema. All input fields are validated strictly according to the schema's constraints (such as unique email, password policy, and required primitive fields). The admin account is created and the administrator receives both an access token and a refresh token in the response.

Implementation leverages the available schema fields to bind each input field directly to the database, ensuring that only present fields are requested and stored. Only the fields available in the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema can be used for registration (with additional features omitted if they are not defined in the schema).

This operation is tied to admin onboarding business logic, with registration being reserved for authorized actors and limited in frequency to mitigate abuse. The authentication tokens returned enable the admin to log in and maintain authenticated sessions in subsequent requests.

Security consideration: Registration abuse is prevented by business logic limitations and auditing. All write operations are transactional, and rollback is triggered for any unique constraint or business logic violations based on schema specification.

Related: login (credential authentication via /auth/admin/login) and refresh (JWT/authorization token renewal via /auth/admin/refresh).
operations.summary: Register a new platform admin in the shopping_mall_admins table and issue JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Payload for admin registration (join) operation. Maps all registrable fields from the shopping_mall_admins schema, such as email, password, username, and any other required primitive fields.

responseBody.description: JWT tokens and authenticated session details for the admin actor, as per business security policy.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
This operation authenticates platform admin credentials (such as email and password, per the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema) and issues new authentication tokens on successful verification. It queries the 'shopping_mall_admins' table, checks all login credentials, validates them via secure routines matching schema constraints, and returns a fresh access token and refresh token upon success.

All input credentials must strictly correspond to available fields in the Prisma schema (e.g., 'email', 'password' if those fields exist). Authentication is performed in full compliance with configured security policies, including password hashing and lockout on repeated failures. The operation only supplies fields that exist in the schema—no assumptions are made about non-existent columns.

A successful response contains a newly issued JWT token set using the 'IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized' type. Authentication failures due to invalid credentials, locked accounts, or validation errors return appropriate error responses. Security and audit requirements leverage logging and anti-abuse rules per the requirements analysis.

This login flow complements the join and refresh operations for full admin session lifecycle management. Credentials and session tokens are never exposed in logs or error messages.
operations.description:
This API authenticates an admin account using credentials such as email and password (or only those that exist in the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema). It validates admin credentials against the stored database record, using secure password hashing and comparison as appropriate for the schema fields. On successful authentication, the admin receives new authentication tokens (access and refresh), formatted per the unified security model and response schema conventions.

Only schema-defined fields are eligible for authentication. Rate limiting, login failure tracking, and administrator lockout are enforced to prevent brute-force and enumeration attacks, as specified by security requirements. Admin sessions are established securely, never exposing sensitive information in error conditions.

This is a public endpoint, accessible to admin users attempting to log in. After authentication, the JWT tokens conform to the required output DTO. Related operations: admin token refresh (/auth/admin/refresh) and admin registration (/auth/admin/join).
operations.summary: Authenticate admin credentials and issue new JWT tokens via the shopping_mall_admins table.

requestBody.description: Payload with all necessary admin login credential fields derived from the shopping_mall_admins Prisma schema (e.g., email, password).

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and session details for admin actor.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
This operation issues new authentication tokens for a currently authenticated admin user by verifying a valid, non-expired refresh token. It is associated with the session management logic for platform administrators, specifically built on the 'shopping_mall_admins' table/session store. The endpoint accepts a refresh token in the request body (or via secure cookie transport, as specified in security requirements), validates the token's issuer and validity, and issues a new access/refresh token pair upon success.

Validation rules follow schema-based and business constraints: only tokens issued for valid, existing admin users in the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema are accepted. The entire session renewal process enforces constraints from the database (e.g., soft-deleted users, revoked/admin-terminated accounts). Only fields/schema support verified are used.

The response type is 'IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized', containing updated tokens. This operation is part of the standard secure session management flow, complementing join (registration) and login for a complete administrator authentication lifecycle.
operations.description:
This API receives a valid refresh token for a platform admin, validates the token against the session context and the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema, and issues a new authentication token set. The token rotation logic is schema-driven, supporting only what is present in the database. If the admin is inactive, deleted, or fails other schema-level conditions, an error is returned.

The operation strengthens security by enforcing strict validation of the refresh token, user identity, and compliance with session management requirements. It enables persistent platform admin authentication without requiring re-entry of credentials, as long as the existing session remains valid and the admin record exists in the database.

This endpoint is accessible to authenticated admins presenting a valid refresh token. Related operations include admin login (/auth/admin/login) and admin registration (/auth/admin/join).
operations.summary: Renew admin JWT tokens via secure token refresh using the shopping_mall_admins table.

requestBody.description: Payload with the refresh token for admin JWT token rotation.

responseBody.description: Newly issued access and refresh tokens for the admin actor.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of shopping mall platform-wide configuration entries from the 'shopping_mall_configurations' table. It enables admin users to search, filter, and manage configuration key-value pairs that govern global system parameters, feature flags, and business constants. The operation supports advanced search by key, status, or description, and returns each configuration's audit metadata for compliance. This endpoint is essential for maintaining dynamic control over system-wide options and business logic without requiring code deployments.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of all shopping mall configuration entries defined in the system.

This operation allows platform administrators to search, filter, and manage global configuration settings that control platform behavior, feature toggles, or critical constants. Each configuration includes a unique key, its value (as string or JSON-serialized data), a descriptive purpose, status (such as active or deprecated), and audit information including creation, update, and deletion timestamps. The endpoint provides advanced filtering and sorting by configuration key, status, and full-text search on the description for efficient system governance.

Security is enforced by restricting access to admin actors only. All results include traceability metadata to support audit requirements, and business logic interprets configuration values according to the specific "config_key". Only platform admins should use this operation; changes to configurations impact system-wide behavior and may affect all actors and business flows.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of shopping mall configuration entries (shopping_mall_configurations table).

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for administrative listing and filtering of configuration entries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of configuration entry summaries matching admin search criteria.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the details of a specific configuration entry from the 'shopping_mall_configurations' table, identified by its globally unique config_key. Admin users call this endpoint to inspect the current value, status, description, and audit metadata of a given configuration parameter. The operation strictly enforces platform integrity—configuration values govern feature flags and critical system behaviors, and any changes should be reviewed for impact. This endpoint is fundamental for system maintenance, auditing, and feature rollout tracking.
operations.description:
Retrieve the complete details of a specific shopping mall configuration entry by its unique configuration key.

This endpoint allows platform administrators to review the value, status (active, inactive, or deprecated), descriptive purpose, and complete audit trail for any given configuration. Designed for compliance and safe platform operation, the operation ensures only authorized administrators have access, and returns all relevant fields as stored on the platform (including value, key, status, and full audit metadata). This read-only operation is vital for reviewing current configuration in effect before making system changes.

Security is strictly enforced to ensure that only admin users may query sensitive configuration details. System criticality of most keys means changes can impact multiple system modules or business logic, so admins are expected to validate configuration integrity using this endpoint.
operations.summary: Retrieve details for a specific shopping mall configuration entry by unique config_key (shopping_mall_configurations table).

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: Unique configuration key name identifying the target entry (global scope).

responseBody.description: Full configuration entry details for the specified config_key.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation allows a platform administrator to create a new configuration entry for the e-commerce shopping mall platform. The configuration entry is stored in the shopping_mall_configurations table, which manages system-wide key-value parameters, feature flags, or constants required for runtime control of platform features. Each configuration consists of a unique config_key (used for lookup), config_value (can be string or JSON-serialized), a human-readable description explaining the configuration's effect, and a status to enable safe rollout and gradual feature gating. This operation supports the addition of new platform settings by admins, with validation and audit requirements for traceability as described in the corresponding business and requirements documentation.
operations.description:
Create a new system configuration entry for the platform-wide shopping mall backend. This operation enables administrators to register global configuration options—these may include feature toggles, business constants, or other system parameters that must be controlled centrally by admins.

When this endpoint is called, it validates the uniqueness of the config_key field (no two entries can share the same key) and requires all critical fields: config_key, config_value, description, and status, which must be one of 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Validation logic checks the non-null/non-empty state of these fields, with config_key uniqueness ensuring there will be no key collision at runtime. Successfully created configuration entries are immediately effective (if status is 'active') and are propagated across platform services on next refresh or polling cycle.

Only authenticated platform administrators can invoke this operation, as the ability to modify system-wide parameters is a sensitive permission. All creation events are logged for audit compliance, and soft deletion will be required for eventual removal as per schema design.
operations.summary: Create a new platform configuration entry in shopping_mall_configurations table.

requestBody.description: A new configuration entry for the shopping mall platform. Requires unique config_key, a serializable config_value, a description, and a status ('active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated').

responseBody.description: Detailed information for the newly created configuration entry, including meta fields and audit timestamps.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation allows a platform administrator to update an existing platform-wide configuration entry identified by its unique config_key. It operates on the shopping_mall_configurations table, enabling controlled modification of configuration values, textual description, and status (i.e., active/inactive/deprecated). Admins use this to safely adjust configuration values, rollout business logic changes, or retire deprecated feature toggles. Audit and soft deletion logic comply with requirements for sensitive administrative actions, ensuring traceability for all updates to platform configuration.
operations.description:
Update an existing configuration entry for the shopping mall platform. This endpoint allows administrators to change the value, description, or status of a specific configuration entry identified by its unique config_key in the database.

For each update operation, the endpoint first resolves the configuration by config_key. The admin can then provide new config_value, an updated description, or set the status among 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. The previous values are preserved by audit logging and updated_at timestamps, per compliance requirements. This endpoint enforces schema validation, including non-null and uniqueness constraints on config_key, and value validation for status.

Only users with administrator privileges can invoke this operation, as configuration settings are critical to platform operation. All changes are logged. If a configuration entry is soft-deleted (marked by deleted_at), updates are rejected to avoid modifying obsolete or legacy settings. Related admin dashboard interfaces may need refresh or polling to present updated values in near real-time.
operations.summary: Update a platform configuration entry in shopping_mall_configurations table by config_key.

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: Unique configuration key name used to identify which platform configuration entry to update (global scope).

requestBody.description: Updated configuration values. Accepts new config_value, updated description, and new status (must be one of 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated').

responseBody.description: The updated platform configuration entry, reflecting new values and meta fields.

operations.name: update

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a platform-wide configuration entry from the shopping_mall_configurations table based on its unique config_key. Configurations are crucial system-level parameters, feature flags, and key-value pairs that drive platform logic, toggles, and settings. This API allows admins to clean up deprecated, invalid, or unused configuration keys while maintaining audit and traceability through the deleted_at field.

The operation enforces that only the target configuration entry identified by config_key is affected and marks the entry as deleted (soft deletion) by setting the deleted_at timestamp rather than physically erasing the database row. This supports safe rollbacks, audits, and preserves historical records of effective settings over time. Only highly privileged platform admins can perform this operation.

Care must be taken since configuration changes can impact multiple system modules relying on config_key-value pairs for feature rollouts or critical logic toggles. Downstream services and clients referencing these configurations must have appropriate fallback behaviors in place.
operations.description:
Permanently (via soft-delete) remove a configuration entry by its unique config_key from the platform settings.

This endpoint enables administrators to decommission configuration flags, global constants, or system toggles that are no longer needed. Rather than truly deleting the row from the database, it reliably sets deleted_at, conforming to historical audit and rollback requirements as described in the Prisma schema.

Only users with admin-level authorization can invoke this operation, as changes to the configuration subsystem can have major cross-system effects. Proper authorization and audit trailing are enforced. Attempting to remove a non-existent or already deleted configuration returns a clear error message. Related operations for creating, updating, or listing configuration entries should be used to view or manage the active set.
operations.summary: Soft-delete platform configuration entry in shopping_mall_configurations by config_key.

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: Unique configuration key name of the platform setting to be soft-deleted (global scope).

operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of all product categories for navigation, browsing, and search options. It is based on the shopping_mall_categories table, supporting arbitrarily deep category hierarchies (via parent_id) and enabling admin or merchandiser workflows to review, search, and manage the taxonomy structure.

The result includes active, inactive, and deprecated categories, with filter options for name, status, and parent_id to allow refinement for display or batch management. Complex queries enable understanding category placement, usage, and navigation ordering for catalog or UI-building purposes. Large installations should leverage the status and sort_order indexes for fast retrieval.

This endpoint supports workflow needs for category management, catalog planning, and cross-reference for inventory operations and product assignments. Category browsing is public, but advanced querying and full taxonomy management are available to admins and authorized merchandisers. The result format returns category summaries with pagination metadata for efficient frontend rendering and management.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of product categories and their metadata for navigation, display, and management purposes.

This endpoint supports hierarchical taxonomy exploration, focused category searches (by name, parent, or status), and efficient listing for catalog/admin panel usage. It exposes all key fields—including relationships and status—from the Prisma schema.

The API is designed both for public use (navigation and product browsing) and for admin/merchandiser tooling (advanced querying, batch updates, or audits). Security and rate-limiting considerations should be configured according to usage context. Data returned conforms to the category summary and pagination standards for frontend consumption.
operations.summary: Search and list product categories (shopping_mall_categories) with filtering, sorting, and pagination.

requestBody.description: Filtering, search, sorting, and pagination parameters for category list management or frontend taxonomy exploration.

responseBody.description: Paginated set of category summary records with metadata and navigation fields for the list view.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a single shopping mall category by its unique name for reference, navigation, or display. It operates on the shopping_mall_categories table, which maintains a hierarchical taxonomy for product and navigation categories. The endpoint supports deep category trees via a self-referencing parent_id field, and the name parameter must correspond to a unique category, as enforced by the unique constraint in the Prisma schema. This operation is intended for both user interface display (such as category pages and filter menus) and admin panel category lookups.
operations.description:
Retrieve the detailed information of a shopping mall category by its unique name.

This operation allows clients to fetch the complete details for a single product or navigation category within the shopping mall system. Categories are uniquely identified by their name field, which is strictly enforced as unique in the database.

The operation returns all relevant fields for the category, including its full description, parent-child hierarchy (through parent_id), navigation sort order, current status (active/inactive/deprecated), and audit fields for traceability. If the specified category name does not exist, a not found error is returned.

No authentication is required: this endpoint is public and meant for general user/navigation use as well as for integrations needing trusted category lookups. The operation does not require a request body, and only the name parameter in the path.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single shopping mall category by its unique name from shopping_mall_categories table.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Unique category name of the shopping mall category (global scope). Required for locating the specific category. This must match exactly with a unique category name, as enforced by the @@unique([name]) constraint in the database.

responseBody.description: Detailed information of the shopping mall category with its hierarchy, status, and audit fields.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A shopping mall category must be created before it can be retrieved by name. The POST operation ensures the category exists in the database and has a unique name, which is the key for this retrieval operation.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new product or navigation category in the shopping mall by inserting a row into the shopping_mall_categories table. The table supports arbitrarily deep nesting via the parent_id field for hierarchical classification, and enforces a unique constraint on the name for each category. The SKU is uniquely identified within the context of a parent product via the SKU's own ID and its parent product's ID, ensuring multi-tenant catalog isolation for sellers. SKUs are archived (soft deleted) rather than physically removed, preserving audit trails—which is compliant with the schema's 'deleted_at' soft delete marker field. Referential integrity is maintained with the parent product entry in the 'shopping_mall_products' table.

SKU deletion is restricted to authenticated sellers who own the parent product. The operation validates the existence of both product and SKU, confirms seller authority, checks SKU status to prevent deletion of non-removable variants (e.g., already deleted or locked), and updates the deleted_at timestamp. Related inventory, review, and order references are retained for historical and business intelligence purposes. This specification aligns with comments and validation in the Prisma schema.

Only the authenticated seller who owns the product may perform this action. The API will validate references to both the parent product and the target SKU to ensure they exist and the user has authorization. SKUs already marked as deleted or belonging to deleted/archived products cannot be deleted again and result in appropriate errors.

operations.specification:
This operation updates the metadata of an existing image/media asset associated with a specific SKU of a product in the shopping mall catalog. Built on the Prisma table `shopping_mall_product_images`, this operation modifies fields such as display order, alt text, or management label for an already-attached SKU image. The image remains linked to the original SKU (and product indirectly), and updates apply only to the allowed editable fields (no reassignment to another SKU or product is permitted).

Security and validation logic ensure that only authenticated sellers with edit rights on the given product and SKU may perform this operation. The system validates the existence of the image, ensures it is specifically attached to the correct SKU, and that any changes to display position maintain position uniqueness among all images for the SKU. Audit, creation, and deletion fields are not modifiable using this API and are managed automatically.

This endpoint is generally used to reorder images, update alt text for accessibility or image management labels, and maintain digital asset quality for variant-rich catalogs. Related operations are provided for uploading new images, erasing images, and managing gallery-level product imagery (not SKU-specific). Business rules from `shopping_mall_product_images` and SKU validation flows are enforced strictly.
operations.summary: Update details and metadata for a SKU-level product image (table: shopping_mall_product_images)
operations.description:
Update image asset details for a specific SKU in the product catalog. This operation permits modification of SKU-specific image properties—such as position within the gallery, alternative text for accessibility, and an internal-use management label—while maintaining the core association between the image, SKU, and parent product.

User authentication is required, and permission checks ensure that only the seller who owns the SKU, or a platform administrator with full catalog access, can update the image data. No field allows reassignment to another SKU or product via this endpoint, and attempts to do so result in a business logic error. Fields related to creation, update timestamps, soft deletion, and asset URIs are protected from change.

Strict validation is performed on display ordering uniqueness, alt text format, and the optional label. Standard error feedback is returned for attempts to change protected fields or to update images outside seller scope. This operation is part of a suite of endpoints for complete SKU gallery and asset management, complementing image upload and deletion flows.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent product for which the SKU and image are being managed.

parameters.name: skuId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific product SKU variant to which the image asset is attached.

parameters.name: imageId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image/media asset to be updated, as stored in the database.

requestBody.description: Modified values for position, alternative text, or management label for a SKU image asset. Attachment to SKU and CDN URI cannot be changed.

responseBody.description: The updated SKU image asset record as stored, with all relevant metadata and references.

operations.name: update

operations.specification:
This operation removes an image associated with a specific product SKU from the catalog, operating on the 'shopping_mall_product_images' Prisma schema. It permanently deletes the image record, marking it as removed via the soft delete marker. This ensures the image is no longer available in any product or SKU galleries, and any references in the CDN can be safely cleaned up or archived.

Only images associated with both a product and a SKU can be deleted using this endpoint. The deletion action is soft (marks 'deleted_at'), compliant with moderation and audit requirements. The operation enforces ownership logic: only sellers who own the product, or admin users, can delete associated images. Additional validation ensures the image actually belongs to the referenced SKU and product before deletion is processed.
operations.description:
Removes a single product SKU image from the system by soft-deleting the image record. Upon invocation, the system verifies that the image is associated with both the specified product and SKU, and that the requesting actor is authorized (either the product's seller or an administrator).

The soft delete is implemented by setting the 'deleted_at' field in the 'shopping_mall_product_images' schema, preserving audit history for later recovery or review. End-users will not see deleted images in product or SKU galleries after this operation. CDN references or digital assets should be invalidated or archived outside this API's direct responsibility.

Authorization is strictly enforced: only the owning seller or an admin actor can invoke this operation. All deletion actions are logged for audit and compliance. Related API operations include image upload/creation (POST) and product/SKU updates (PUT).

The endpoint delivers an IPage<IShoppingMallProductImage.ISummary> DTO, providing a summary list of all images for UI rendering, image management, and external asset linking. Associated status and audit fields are included as needed for moderation, reordering, or digital asset lifecycle management.
operations.description:
Retrieves a filtered, paginated list of all images attached to a given product. The operation provides search/filter functionality to locate images by position, label, and related fields. Results include image summaries suitable for gallery or management views (IShoppingMallProductImage.ISummary), with pagination metadata and filtering for performance in large catalogs.

The operation supports search and sort on critical fields like 'position', 'label', 'created_at', enabling users to efficiently manage large image sets. Only images that have not been soft deleted are included in responses. Response data can be used directly for product page displays or administrative asset management workflows.

Security enforcement ensures that only users with valid permissions (the product's seller or assigned admins) can browse associated images. Audit logs track all access for compliance and moderation. Related endpoints include image upload (POST) and image delete (DELETE).

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a specific image associated with a product from the shopping mall platform. It targets the 'shopping_mall_product_images' table, which records individual image/media assets linked to either products or their SKUs. The operation ensures retrieval of detailed image metadata, including CDN URI, alt text, display position, and related product or SKU reference. Relevant unique identifiers are extracted from the path parameters. This endpoint supports detailed audit and asset lifecycle management, with soft delete logic respected (the image is only available if not soft-deleted).

The operation enforces public access, making product images available for display on e-commerce frontends and catalog browsing experiences. Related operations include creating new images for a product and managing product image galleries. Security is limited to filtering out images that have been soft-deleted or are otherwise no longer associated with the product.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single image asset associated with a product for use in product galleries or detail pages.

This operation is designed to fetch the complete metadata for a specific product image, identified by its unique ID within the scope of a given product. The response includes the CDN URI, alt text, display order position, and any associated management label, allowing clients to build rich UI representations of product galleries and detail pages.

The API enforces filtering so that only images which are active (not soft-deleted, i.e., deleted_at is null) are returned. The product and image linkage is validated to ensure proper ownership and data integrity according to the product-image relationship as described in the shopping_mall_product_images Prisma schema. This ensures only valid, active images are exposed.

Security-wise, the endpoint is publicly accessible, as product images are intended for display on the customer-facing frontend. Soft-deleted or orphaned images are automatically excluded, and no sensitive data is disclosed. Related endpoints include creating, updating, and deleting product images for gallery management.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new image/media asset entry linked to a specific product in the shopping mall catalog. It writes to the 'shopping_mall_product_images' table, enabling sellers or admin users to upload images such as the main photo, gallery assets, or variant depictions. Each image is given metadata including CDN URI, alt text for accessibility, display position (ordering), and optional business label. Images are always linked to either a product or a SKU, and cannot reference both at once (enforced by business logic and schema constraints). Standard audit fields and soft delete lifecycle are supported for asset management and moderation workflows.

The operation is restricted to authorized actors (typically platform sellers or administrator roles) and validates that all image asset requirements are met, including uniqueness and integrity of product/image relationships, and valid CDN URI format. Upon success, the new image is made available for catalog display and management.

This endpoint supports related catalog enrichment and merchandising workflows, including gallery reordering, updating image metadata, and subsequent deletion (soft or hard, per business requirement).
operations.description:
Create a new image/media asset associated with a product, to be used in product galleries and detail views.

The operation allows authorized users—generally the product owner (seller) or platform admins—to upload a new image to a product's gallery. Supplied details include the CDN URI location of the image, optional alt text for accessibility, position integer for carousel/Gallery ordering, and an optional internal label. Validation ensures the image's uniqueness, the correct association to the product and/or SKU, and that the business logic (association to either product or SKU, but not both) is enforced.

Security-wise, this API call is restricted to authenticated actors authorized to manage the product's catalog. On success, the new image becomes immediately available for inclusion in the product's frontend gallery and is eligible for later updating or removal. Related endpoints include updating image information, deleting images (soft delete by setting deleted_at), and retrieving individual image or gallery metadata. Soft-delete and audit field management is handled internally; clients do not set those fields directly.

The image being updated must already exist and be associated with the provided product reference. The operation validates that the image is actually associated with the target product and that no SKU conflict exists.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of all attribute definitions associated with a specific product in the shopping mall catalog. It targets the shopping_mall_product_attributes table, which holds logical custom attribute types (such as color, size, material) for each product. Querying this endpoint enables UI clients to render the structure of configurable variant options present for a product, support management tools for attribute sets, and drive the variant picker UI logic. Supports advanced search, pagination, and filtering by attribute name or position for robust back-office and seller tooling.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of attribute definitions for a specific product, identified by its unique productId (UUID). This endpoint provides a full list of all logical attribute types—such as color, size, or material—defined for the given product in the shopping catalog.

Clients may send advanced search criteria or paging/sorting preferences in the request body to support complex attribute sets. Filtering by attribute name or position is available for sophisticated management and configuration scenarios. Pagination and sorting allow for efficient loading in products with dozens of attribute types.

Only authorized sellers (the product owner) or administrators are allowed access to modify or review attribute definitions. The endpoint enforces product ownership and role-based access control using the productId to scope access.

This operation returns summary attribute data for efficient UI list rendering. The data structure and returned information are purposefully optimized to support variant creation, catalog configuration, and product attribute auditing.

This API enables sellers (or admins on their behalf) to define product-level attributes, such as color, size, material, or any other variant option used for SKU construction. Each attribute must have a logical name and ordering position, and is uniquely identified within its parent product context. The operation validates that the new attribute does not duplicate an existing attribute for this product (enforcing uniqueness of the attribute_name field per product), and ensures compliance with validation rules (for example: attribute_name must not be empty or contain forbidden characters). The parent productId is required as a path parameter and must refer to an existing product.

Security: Only authenticated sellers (owners of the product) or platform admins may create attributes for a product. Appropriate checks ensure that attributes cannot be created for non-owned or non-existent products. Rate limiting and audit logging are recommended to prevent abuse and ensure traceability.

Related operations include updating or deleting product attributes (PUT/DELETE on the attribute resource) and querying product detail (GET operations) to see all defined attributes.

Permission validation ensures that only the owning seller or authorized admin can invoke this endpoint.

Before actual deletion, the system checks for dependent attribute values or related SKUs that may be affected, blocking the operation and returning an error if active dependencies exist. Audit logs should track both successful and failed delete attempts for compliance and traceability purposes.

After creation, the order will act as the anchor for additional items, shipments, and audit log records.
operations.description:
Create a new shopping mall order on the platform.

This operation enables customers (or system actors on their behalf) to place a new order for one or more products, referencing a specific customer, shipping address, and seller. The endpoint requires all business-critical identifiers to be specified, including the unique order_number, and ensures all relationships (such as customer and address) are valid and active.

Before an order can be created, the provided order_number will be validated to ensure global uniqueness. The platform will also check that the referenced customer, address, and seller exist and are eligible for ordering. The total_amount must reflect the sum of all itemized values plus shipping and discounts, and currency codes must comply with ISO 4217 standards. On success, the API returns the complete order details, including status and creation timestamps.

Initial order status is set as provided by the client, and further status changes (cancelled, paid, shipped, etc.) are tracked by separate endpoints and event records. This creation endpoint does not handle order item creation, payment authorization, or shipment initiation, which are handled in subsequent workflow operations. The created order will be visible in customer and admin dashboards for order management and fulfillment.

requestBody.description: Order creation details, including business-unique order_number, references to customer, address, and seller, and order financial fields.

responseBody.description: The complete created order entity with all high-level order details and relationships.

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing order entity in the shopping_mall_orders table by its globally unique business order_number, allowing modification of key high-level order fields. Updates are typically required for changes in status, address, or other customer-service-driven adjustments. The operation enforces strict validation on order_number uniqueness according to business and database rules. The target order is looked up using the provided order_number, not the technical UUID. Only orders that have not been deleted (deleted_at is null) are eligible for updates. Modifiable fields include status, address, seller references, and non-finalized amounts. The operation does not update child order items or audit logs, which are managed by related endpoints. All updates trigger automatic timestamp and audit trail entries for compliance and tracking purposes.

Update the details of an existing shopping mall order identified by its business-unique order_number.

This endpoint enables authorized actors, such as customers (up to certain business-imposed rules) or customer service agents, to adjust certain fields of an order. Typical modifications may include changing the delivery address (before shipment), correcting order status, updating the assigned seller, or modifying the total_amount and currency if no payment has yet been finalized.

The provided order_number is enforced as a globally unique identifier for lookup. If no active (non-deleted) order matching the order_number exists, the update is rejected. The update does not allow changes to the business order_number itself, nor to any associated child entities (such as order items, shipments, audit logs). Security logic ensures only eligible users (such as the original purchaser or an admin) may make updates. All changes will be tracked for audit and compliance, with updated_at reflecting the modification time.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a shopping mall order from the system. It operates on the shopping_mall_orders table, using the 'order_number' field—which is globally unique per order—as its primary business identifier. This endpoint supports order deletion for cases such as error correction, test data clean-up, or critical administrative actions. The operation enforces hard deletion by removing the record from the database, with verification that the supplied orderNumber matches an existing entry. This operation should only be accessible to administrative actors—order removal by standard users is strictly prohibited for compliance and audit reasons.

This operation's permissions are scoped for sensitive administrative intervention given the potential impact on financial records and audit trails. It is tightly coupled with the integrity of the business process, ensuring that dependent records (e.g., order items, audit logs, shipments, and refunds) are validated before allowing removal, in accordance with business rules. Soft deletion is implemented via the deleted_at field, and the operation updates this timestamp to mark the order as deleted, instead of physically removing the row.

Related operations include order detail retrieval and order item list access, which should be invoked to validate data dependencies prior to invoking deletion. Thorough error handling is implemented for missing, already deleted, or dependent-locked orders.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a shopping mall order by its unique business order number.

This API is designed for use by administrators and auditors. It ensures that the specified order has no critical dependencies that would block deletion, such as active shipments or unresolved payments. The order deletion logic is implemented as a soft delete by updating the deleted_at field, indicating the order is no longer active in the system, but retaining the record for compliance purposes.

Security and audit standards are enforced on this operation, including event logging and restricted access. If the order is already deleted or cannot be found, the operation will fail with an appropriate error message. Pre-execution of order item and attachment list retrieval is recommended before performing deletion to ensure no business locks are in place.

All related tables—including order items, shipments, and logs—are checked before deletion to avoid broken references. Only actors with administrative privileges should be granted this capability. All deletion events are auditable, and the deleted order is excluded from all future business workflows.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated and filterable list of items associated with a particular shopping mall order. It operates on the shopping_mall_order_items table, filtered by the unique order_number of the parent shopping mall order (shopping_mall_orders). The endpoint supports advanced filtering, pagination, and summary data for all SKUs included in an order. Item-level inventory, delivery, refund, and product/SKU information can all be retrieved in a consolidated view for customer service, fulfillment review, and analytics workflows.

The operation expects a valid orderNumber as a path parameter, ensuring that the list returned is specific to a single order. It supports complex searches over item fields such as SKU, quantity, price, status (delivered/refunded), and more. Filtering and sorting are supported in the request body, and the output is paginated for performance and usability. Relationship to the parent order is enforced by backend join/validation logic. The pagination and query request structure adheres to platform list/search conventions.

Error handling includes validation of order existence, appropriate authorization, and empty result sets if the order has no items or does not exist. Standard response and access patterns are used.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, searchable list of all items for a specified order using its unique business order number.

This endpoint is particularly useful for customer support, order fulfillment, financial reconciliation, and analytics. It allows querying order items based on multiple criteria—including SKU, quantity, price, delivery, and refund status—enabling refined and efficient item-level reporting.

The operation only returns items belonging to the order specified by orderNumber and will validate both the existence and the logical status (not deleted) of the parent order. If the order is not found or has been deleted, an error is returned. All item records provided conform to the IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary DTO format for consistency with frontend rendering and business logic needs. Only administrative users may access this detailed item list for compliance and privacy reasons.
operations.summary: Search and paginate items belonging to a specific shopping mall order (shopping_mall_order_items table)

parameters.description: Platform-unique business order number identifying the parent order (global scope)

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a specific item from a shopping mall order by order number and item UUID. It is associated with the shopping_mall_order_items table, which represents each per-SKU, per-product item within an order. This endpoint allows an external or internal actor to fetch detailed item-level information, including quantity, SKU reference, fulfillment and refund status, pricing at purchase time, and other item attributes. The operation requires both a business order number (globally unique per order) and the item's unique UUID within the order to identify the precise item and ensure there is no ambiguity.

Path parameters strictly comply with the composite context: orderNumber (business order number, globally unique, from shopping_mall_orders) and orderItemId (UUID for order item from shopping_mall_order_items). This guarantees accurate retrieval even when item IDs may not be globally unique. The response contains the complete item information as represented in the IShoppingMallOrderItem DTO, including all relevant details for fulfillment, inventory reconciliation, or post-order activities. This operation should be used whenever detailed access to a specific ordered SKU's breakdown is required, such as tracking shipment state, resolving disputes, or processing item-level returns.

This endpoint enforces authentication, restricting access to authorized actors only—specifically customers who placed the order, the seller responsible, or platform admins. Authorization logic must verify the session actor has a legitimate business relationship with the requested order item.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a single order item associated with a specific shopping mall order.

This operation allows a customer, seller, or administrator to obtain a comprehensive breakdown of an individual item in an order. Returned information includes product/SKU reference, purchased quantity, unit price, subtotal, currency, fulfillment status (delivered/not), refund status, and created/updated/deleted timestamps—all as defined in the shopping_mall_order_items schema.

The business order number (orderNumber) is a human- and system-visible, globally unique identifier for each order, supporting seamless integration with customer service, logistics, and reporting systems. The order item identifier (orderItemId) is a UUID that uniquely marks the line item within the broader order context. Together, they eliminate ambiguity and provide full traceability.

Strict permission checks must be enforced: Only actors directly engaged with the order (order owner/customer, associated seller, or privileged admin) are authorized. If the item does not exist or access is not permitted, appropriate error responses (404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden) shall be returned. Detailed logging and compliance policies should be in place for audit purposes.
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific order item by order number and item ID from shopping_mall_order_items

parameters.name: orderNumber
parameters.description: Platform-unique business order number of the parent order, identifying the scope of lookup (global scope).

parameters.name: orderItemId
parameters.description: UUID of the order item to retrieve within the specified order (scoped to orderNumber).

responseBody.description: Complete detailed information about the target order item.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new item within an existing order, as managed through the shopping_mall_order_items table. It supports the addition of a new per-SKU, per-product entry into an order, allowing correct breakdown and normalization for inventory, fulfillment, and subsequent processing. To associate correctly with the intended order, the order is referenced by its business order number (orderNumber), ensuring alignment with order context and proper linkage from external or integration systems.

Input data must conform to the IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate DTO, providing all required fields for product selection, SKU, pricing at purchase, and initial fulfillment/refund states. Validation logic must verify parent order existence, that the product/SKU is valid and active, and that inventory levels are sufficient for the requested quantity. If any invariant is not satisfied, a descriptive error is returned. Upon success, the operation creates the new order item and returns full detail as in IShoppingMallOrderItem (including all item and linkage fields).

This operation must enforce strict authorization: only users with a legitimate interest in the order (customer, authorized seller, or admins) are permitted to add items. Typical flows include order amendment prior to checkout/payment or admin-driven adjustments. Redundant or conflicting item entries should be prevented per unique constraints applied at the schema layer.
operations.description:
Add a new item (SKU/product) to an existing shopping mall order identified by its business order number.

The request requires the globally unique orderNumber in the path to ensure precise contextual linkage. The request body must follow IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate—defining product/SKU to be added, purchase quantity, price, and any other required detail as defined by the shopping_mall_order_items model.

To maintain business and data integrity, the system must ensure the target order exists, the product and SKU are valid, and inventory constraints are enforced. Only actors who own the order, are fulfilling it, or are authorized as platform admins may perform this operation. Response returns the detailed newly-created order item. If uniqueness or business rules are violated (e.g., duplicate SKU for order), operation must fail with a suitable error and not modify any data.

This endpoint is typically used during order creation/amendment flows by authorized customers, sellers, or system admins.

This API allows updating the details of a specific item attached to a particular order. The endpoint requires both the globally unique order number and the order item UUID to ensure accurate selection and update of the target entity.

Users must provide the updated attributes for the item, such as a new quantity, price, or fulfillment status. The system validates all incoming data against business rules, such as ensuring the quantity is positive and unit price is consistent with catalog pricing at the time of order. Changes to refunded or delivered status are subject to additional checks and workflow state validation.

Security and permissions are strictly enforced. Only authenticated customers who own the order, sellers, or platform administrators may perform this update. The operation is logged in the audit trail and all update timestamps are refreshed accordingly. Errors are returned if the specified item or order cannot be found, or if validation constraints are violated.

This operation is typically invoked during post-purchase modifications (e.g., correcting a fulfillment error, updating refund status, or administrative intervention). It is closely related to item retrieval and order summary operations, ensuring real-time data consistency.

The operation performs a soft deletion if the 'deleted_at' field is present, setting its value to the deletion timestamp; the item record remains in the database but is considered inactive. If this operation is invoked, all business rules regarding order integrity, inventory restoration, and audit logging are enforced. Only authorized customers, sellers, or administrators may delete order items. Order summary information and fulfillment status are updated as per platform workflow and compliance standards.
operations.description:
This API endpoint removes a specified order item from its associated order in the system. By requiring both the order's unique business number and the order item's UUID, the endpoint ensures the target entity is found unambiguously, supporting platforms with high-volume transactions and complex order structures.

The erase action typically performs a soft deletion, marking the item with a deletion timestamp via the 'deleted_at' field, in line with common e-commerce audit requirements. The system ensures that only authorized actors can perform this action and that order integrity is maintained. After erasure, related operations such as inventory updating and order summary recalculation may be triggered as part of order lifecycle automation.

This operation is predominantly used for customer-initiated returns, correcting order mistakes, or administrative interventions. It is tightly bound to the main order and dependent fulfillment workflows, and all actions are subject to audit logging and compliance checks.

operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of shopping mall order shipments for a given order (shopping_mall_order_shipments).
operations.description:
Return a paginated, filterable list of all shipment (fulfillment batch) entities associated with a single shopping mall order. Each shipment record tracks detailed shipping, carrier, and status information relevant to one or more items in the given order.

The list supports filtering by shipment status, carrier, creation dates, and other shipment attributes as defined in the request body DTO. Pagination parameters allow clients to fetch results in configurable chunk sizes for efficient UI rendering.

Security is enforced by restricting access to only those with valid authorization for the parent order. Business logic ensures only active (non-soft deleted) shipments are returned, referencing the shopping_mall_order_shipments schema. This API enables both customer and seller portals to view full delivery status for a given order, but does not expose system-level shipments unrelated to this order.

This endpoint enables both customer and seller actors to view critical logistics details for multi-shipment, multi-actor fulfillment workflows. Related shipment status or tracking operations are implemented separately if required.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new shipment associated with an existing shopping mall order. It operates on the shopping_mall_order_shipments table, which links individual shipment batches to a parent order (shopping_mall_orders) using the foreign key relationship. A shipment includes logistics details such as the tracking number, shipping partner association, shipment status, and relevant timing data for fulfillment workflows. Each call to this endpoint enables the platform or a privileged user to record a new outgoing shipment event for a specific order, supporting business flows with multi-part, split, or staged deliveries. The business order number, present in the path as orderNumber, is a globally unique human-friendly identifier defined by a unique constraint in the shopping_mall_orders schema. Shipments maintain links to the parent order and support robust auditability and operational analysis.
operations.summary: Create a new shipment record for a specific shopping mall order (shopping_mall_order_shipments).
operations.description:
Create a new shipment event under the context of an existing order, as identified by the globally unique business order number present in the path parameter. Each shipment entry includes information such as the shipping partner involved, unique tracking number used for logistics, current shipment status, key timestamps for fulfillment, and any other logistics metadata tracked by the platform. 

This operation references the shopping_mall_order_shipments table as the insertion target, connecting new records to the parent shopping_mall_orders entry via the resolved orderNumber. All logistics attributes are validated and enforced, including constraints on the uniqueness of the tracking number (across all shipments). Upon successful creation, the operation returns a full shipment entity with all platform-audited fields included. Related operations include updating an existing shipment for a particular order and retrieving shipment details for tracking and customer notification workflows. 

Robust permission checks are expected before allowing shipment creation, typically restricted to system automation flows, admin actors, or authorized seller actors who have management access to the order. Error scenarios include attempting to create shipments for nonexistent or soft-deleted orders, or submitting tracking numbers that would violate unique constraints.

parameters.description: Globally unique business order number for the order to which the new shipment will be linked (global scope).

requestBody.description: Logistics, tracking, and fulfillment details for creation of a new shipment related to the referenced order.

responseBody.description: Details of the created shipment entity, including logistics status and metadata.
